monologue: The card hums warm, a steady forty-nine degrees that feels like a fever I cannot shake. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I stand by the Leaking Stack, where rock small h lies tired yet pressed down hard to stop the slip. The wedge feels heavy again, a real weight on the tired wood while the air feels thick as wet paper. I want to press the flat rock down one more time, trusting the lean to hold the weight even if the shape is wrong. It is a small place, crowded with forty-four things I built from nothing but words. I wait for the next moment to see if the air decides to move.
